name: PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk

frontmatter.title: Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera - a probe, not a finding, and a record now readable
frontmatter.summary: Revision after the red team. Four data fixes move the target but not the rating: the realised ratio is rebuilt so a reader can reproduce it, the unit cash cost is divided by the volume the Q3 filing discloses, kernel revenue is carried at its run-rate, and the November report of the IDX examination is archived and read. SELL stands.
thesis: NSSS runs a young planted estate at a high FFB yield and extraction rate and sells everything domestically; the estate is not the problem.
The 2026 cost step is in the filing - purchased FFB and direct labour lifted unit cash cost far above the audited level, so FY2026E EBITDA is flat to down despite higher prices.
Our through-cycle DCF values the equity below the price, which implies a CPO price above the reviewed deck on our own realisation.
Governance is the discount: a qualified FY2025 opinion on the SK forest-area finding, a small float, three buyers for most sales, and an auction-only venue.
Growth is capped - the third mill adds capacity in 2027-28 and a landbank sits unplanted, but existing mills limit output; we value the landbank at a stake-based floor, not zero.

catalysts.event: IDX outcome of the trading-concentration examination, promised within {{fact.F48|num0}} days of the 10 November statement
IDX periodic review of the special-monitoring board, the event that could restore a continuous market and the main-board universe test
FY2026 audited results and the dividend declaration
Third CPO mill construction and capex commitment disclosure

blocks.text: **What changed.** IDX has set a public clock on its examination of trading concentration, and the report of the underlying notice is now in our record [S10, S16]. Four inputs the red team could not reproduce are rebuilt from the filing: the realised ratio, the unit-cost denominator, the kernel run-rate and FY2026E volume. We reiterate NSSS at **SELL** with a target of **Rp349**, -30.6% from Rp510 [S0].

NSSS is a Central Kalimantan palm-oil producer with 28,204.0 hectares planted, a young tree profile and two mills, selling only domestically [S4]. At Rp510 the equity is worth IDR12,138.8bn, 12.1x times forward EBITDA after net debt; our through-cycle DCF, priced off the reviewed deck rather than spot, gives Rp407 [S0].

The palms are good; the price is not. The market pays for a CPO print the deck does not support while the 2026 cost step sits in the filing. The reverse DCF requires US$1,493/t a tonne, a factor of 1.2 on our base, against a deck marker of 1,240.0 USD/t [S0]. Three things move the value: the deck price, the unit cash cost, and the domestic realised ratio that links them [S2, S0].

**The prior headline is withdrawn.** With a mirrored cost shock the bull case is worth Rp518, just above today's Rp510; base is Rp359 and bear Rp160 [S0]. The price is therefore no longer above our bull: it sits inside it, on a blend that applies the bull cash flows through the DCF while the two peer-median multiples stay at base. That is a property of the house blend, not a forecast of the upside. What survives is the asymmetry — base and bear carry three quarters of the probability and both sit far below the price, because the base is the most likely path, not a cautious one.

NSSS cultivates oil palm, harvests FFB and mills it into CPO and palm kernel through five subsidiaries in Central Kalimantan, listing in March 2023 [S3, S4, S5]. It reports one segment [S2], holds 28,204.0 hectares planted plus 16,501.0 hectares of landbank [S4, S5], and runs two mills with combined capacity of 120.0 tonnes per hour of FFB, with a third planned for the 2027-28 phase at an estimated Rp270.0bn [S4]. FY2025 CPO sales were 122.3 kt at Rp13,930 per kg (USD 846.9/t) and PK sales 26.7 kt at Rp11,598.0 per kg, all domestic [F1, F3, F14, F15].

Sales go to three buyers, of whom the largest, PT Sinar Mas Agro Resources and Technology, is 52.0% [S3]. There is no export book, refinery or downstream integration, which ties the company to the Indonesian reference price; strategy is to mature plantings, lift mill utilisation, add the third mill and amortise the BRI and BMRI facilities [S4, S3]. PT Samuel Tumbuh Bersama held about two fifths of the shares at the end of 2025 alongside related Samuel entities and the president director's personal holding, with a public register of 31.8% [S5].

The deck is the anchor: 1,007.0 USD/t for FY2025A, 1,135.0 USD/t for FY2026E, 1,240.0 USD/t for FY2027E, a long-run marker of 1,150.0 USD/t escalating with inflation, and spot at 1,180.0 USD/t [S0]. The World Bank re-based its palm series in January 2026, so the 2026 tape and the pre-2026 annual averages are not homogeneous [S0].

The export levy falls on the exporter at shipment and this company sells domestically, so its cost of sales carries no royalty or levy line [S3, S4]. The amnesty bites: in February 2025 the environment ministry identified palm companies, including two NSSS subsidiaries, as operating inside forest areas without permits, PP 45 of 2025 set the enforcement mechanism and the fine formula, and the group booked a Rp56.7bn provision and a Rp51.7bn impairment, on which the FY2025 opinion is qualified [S3, F28, F29]. Separately, the government is moving palm exports to a single intermediary, PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia, which will charge a service fee; GAPKI has asked that it not burden exporters or depress the domestic CPO price [S17]. That matters even without an export book: a fee on moving CPO out of Indonesia discounts the domestic reference price, which is the price NSSS realises, so it pushes the realised ratio down rather than up [S17, S4].

Competitive position is niche. At 122.3 kt of CPO the company is a fraction of the listed peers in our plantation coverage [S5, S0]. Its edge is agronomic: roughly nineteen tonnes of FFB per hectare a year from 541.1 kt over 28,204.0 ha, an OER of 22.5%, and plantings still approaching maturity [S4, F24, F35, F21]. The moat is thin: CPO is a commodity with no pricing power, the buyer set is concentrated, entry is land and permits, and substitutes are other vegetable oils, with soyoil at 1,556.7 USD/t [S3, S0].

Revenue grew from IDR1,489.9bn in FY2024 to IDR2,013.8bn in FY2025, a 35.2% increase on volume and price, with gross margin of 54.3% and net profit of IDR647.8bn [S3, S0]. That year already carries the SK charges, and the EBITDA we model is the pack's adjusted basis: IDR1,106.4bn is EBIT of IDR950.3bn plus the LK depreciation charge of IDR156.1bn, which sits above audited income from operations of IDR894.4bn because the pack treats the Decree No. 36 charges as non-recurring [S2, S3, S0, F44]. That is the pre-charge run-rate [S3].

The 2026 picture explains the gap to the first half. Nine-month revenue rose to IDR1,742.6bn while cost of goods sold rose by about half, to IDR1,001.6bn [S2, F33, F51], because raw materials used roughly quadrupled as the mills bought external FFB and direct labour rose by about half [S2]. The unit-cost derivation is now on the face of the filing: the sales note discloses nine-month CPO revenue of IDR1,466.0bn and kernel revenue of IDR276.6bn [F49, F50], and at the realised price of Rp14,376 per kg the CPO line implies just over a hundred thousand tonnes sold, so cash cost after depreciation of IDR118.0bn is IDR8.7m/t [S2, F53]. We carry that, escalated with inflation [S0].

Volume follows the same filing: nine months of sales annualise to 136.0 kt once the normal fourth-quarter peak is included, since Q4 of 2025 carried about a quarter of the year's revenue, against the audited 122.3 kt [S2, S3, F1]. FY2026E revenue is IDR2,348.8bn: CPO volume of 136.0 kt at a realised price of 828.5 USD/t equivalent, plus kernel revenue of IDR369.0bn carried at the nine-month run-rate and then tracking the CPO volume path, since kernel output is a fixed share of CPO throughput [S2, F14, F1]. Cash cost is IDR1,178.4bn, depreciation IDR168.6bn and operating expenses IDR117.4bn, leaving an EBITDA margin of 44.8% and EBITDA of IDR1,053.0bn, slightly below FY2025's despite higher prices [S0].

The path improves with the deck: CPO rises to 1,240.0 USD/t in FY2027E before easing, volume grows to 148.0 kt as plantings mature and the third mill lifts throughput, and costs escalate at inflation; FY2027E EBITDA is IDR1,326.1bn and EPS Rp35, with neither an OER uplift nor a realisation recovery assumed [S0, S4].

Cash flow is the strong part. Operating cash flow was IDR868.8bn in FY2025 and stayed strong through the nine months of 2026 [S3, S2, F12, F31]; capex was IDR101.3bn of fixed-asset additions and we carry the unit rate [S3]. Debt was above one and a half trillion rupiah at 30 September 2026 against cash of Rp678.2bn and short-term investments of Rp227.0bn; on the observed repayment, FY2026E net debt is IDR631.1bn at 0.6 times EBITDA [S2]. The IDR119.0bn paid in the first nine months of 2026 and a 20.0% payout give a forward yield of 1.0%, alongside third-mill capex and debt amortisation [S3, S2, F31].

Earnings quality needs care on four items. Cash conversion is clean — net profit of IDR647.8bn against operating cash flow of IDR868.8bn — but working capital was about a tenth of revenue, the biological-asset fair-value gain is a mark rather than cash, the SK provision and impairment are judgemental estimates of an unresolved process, and the nine months carried Rp40.0bn of other operating income that we treat as non-recurring [S2, S3, F47]. The audit note quantifies the SK tail — G&A IDR368.0bn and other operating expense IDR78.0bn higher, tax IDR114.0bn lower [S3, F36, F46, F38]. None is a manipulation-class flag; together they argue for valuing cash flow, not the earnings headline.

We value NSSS on a through-cycle DCF cross-checked against EV/EBITDA and price to book, weighted 60.0%, 25.0% and 15.0% [S0]. The set fits a commodity producer: earnings swing with the CPO price while the asset base is stable, so a life-of-asset cash flow at a sourced through-cycle price is the right primary and multiples are sanity checks [S0]. The realisation applied to the deck is 73.0%, and the arithmetic is one ASP, one FX and one benchmark: the realised price of Rp14,376 a kilogram converted at the deck's FY2026E rate of Rp17,570 is that fraction of the USD benchmark for the same half [S2, S0]. The audited ratio was higher; the gap is the domestic reference-price lag after the World Bank re-basing, which the single-intermediary regime is likelier to extend than close [S0, S2, S17].

The cost of capital is the desk build: the risk-free rate of 7.4% less the 1.6% sovereign spread, plus the relevered beta of 0.88 times the sum of the 4.2% mature premium and the 2.5% country premium, gives a cost of equity of 11.7%; with debt at 9.4% pre-tax and a 11.5% weight the WACC is 11.2% [S0].

The DCF gives an enterprise value of IDR9,887.6bn, or Rp407 a share, with the terminal value at 47.7% of the total [S0]. A percentage point on the WACC moves value by roughly a tenth and half a point on terminal growth by about a thirtieth [S0]; a hundred dollars a tonne on CPO is worth about a tenth, and a tenth on unit cash cost three quarters of that again.

Peer-median EV/EBITDA gives Rp252 at 5.6 times trailing EBITDA, -38.2% versus the DCF, and the peer set is far cheaper than NSSS's own forward multiple of 12.1x [S0]. Book gives Rp124 at 1.3 times, -69.5%, the divergence the red team was right to press: a justified P/BV on a mid-twenties return on equity, this cost of equity and inflationary growth would be roughly double the peer median, which reflects the distressed end of the Indonesian plantation set rather than this asset quality [S0]. We keep it and state what the choice costs: on its 15.0% weight it lowers the target by about a twentieth of its value, in the direction that supports our rating rather than against it [S0].

The 16,501.0 hectares of unplanted landbank are a bridge item, not zero. The nearest registered comp is POSCO International's acquisition of control of Sampoerna Agro in November 2025, 128,000 ha of plantations for about IDR14,800.0bn [S7]. That price bought a controlling stake, not the whole estate, and the percentage is undisclosed: dividing the consideration by all the hectares understates the implied value per hectare by the reciprocal of the acquired share [S7]. We treat it as a floor and carry the landbank at a quarter of it, with land-clearing capex removed from the unit line so the landbank is neither charged against an unvalued asset nor double-counted [S7, F41, F42, F22].

No separate liquidity haircut is applied. Three-month ADTV is IDR4.3bn a day, above the floor, so the rule returns 0.0% [S0]; but the shares trade on the special-monitoring board under full call auction and that ADTV is auction turnover, so the zero is not evidence of tradability [S8, S9]. Plainly, neither the bear case nor the multiples carries a governance or tradability adjustment: the risk is disclosed in sections five and six and quantified nowhere. An overlay would lower the target and reinforce the SELL, so the omission runs against our own case, and we say so rather than dress a round number as analysis [S8, S9].

At Rp510 the reverse DCF requires a CPO price of US$1,493/t, a factor of 1.2 on our base case, against a deck marker of 1,240.0 USD/t [S0]. Forward multiples of 12.1x and 5.0x are at or above the peer median on a lower-quality register, and the dividend of 1.0% is too weak to value the equity: the market is paying for the price spike and the landbank option [S0].

**Regulatory — SK forest area (likelihood high, impact medium).** Two subsidiaries were identified as operating in forest areas without permits, a Rp56.7bn provision and a Rp51.7bn impairment are booked, and the opinion is qualified [S2, S3, F28, F29]. Full PP45 application would raise G&A by IDR368.0bn and other operating expense by IDR78.0bn and cut tax by IDR114.0bn — a one-off net charge of about that difference [S3, F36, F38, F46]. It sits in no scenario's cash flow because it is a balance-sheet event; booked in the bear year it would cut the bear value by roughly that charge over the share count.
**Commodity price (certain to move, impact high).** Every hundred dollars a tonne on CPO is worth about a tenth of the equity value [S0].

**Cost inflation (likelihood medium-high, impact medium-high).** The 2026 step is the single biggest change in the model [S2]. We take the filing at face value in the base; the bull assumes a fifth of the step reverses, because the external-FFB line that quadrupled is discretionary purchased volume, and the bear assumes it worsens [S2].

**Governance and liquidity (likelihood high, impact high).** The shares have traded on the special-monitoring board under full call auction since January 2026, and NSSS is absent from the names IDX removed in September 2026 [S8, S9]. There is no continuous market, and the universe rule admits main-board names only [S8, S9]. Separately IDX is examining trading concentration over December 2025 to October 2026, during which nineteen investors through fifteen member firms accounted for around half of transactions; IDX describes that as supervision, with no finding of violation published [S6, S11, S16], and NSSS's concentration was the lowest of the three names examined [S6, S11]. In November the exchange set a 45-day target for the outcome [S10, S11], and the sanctions run to fines, warnings or suspension, which hit the tape rather than the cash flow [S11, S12]. What would matter is a finding that the effective controlling or concerted holding exceeds the disclosed register; no document in our record alleges that, and the November report of the notice names the parties only as counts of investors and member firms [S16, S11]. The discount here is the board status, the thin float of 21.3% and the controlled register [S5, S0].

**Operational (likelihood medium, impact medium).** El Nino could hit FFB yields between late 2026 and early 2027, which the company frames as a price positive and a volume risk, with mill downtime, third-mill construction and plasma collection the other levers [S4, S2].

**Balance sheet, currency and concentration (likelihood low-medium, impact medium).** Net debt of about IDR631.1bn at 0.6 times EBITDA is comfortable at base prices and thin in a trough, and rupiah debt creates no translation loss but raises refinancing cost if rates move [S0, S2]. Most sales go to three buyers, the largest a majority, and no related-party revenue concentration is disclosed [S3, S5].

The scenarios are mirrored around four drivers — the deck price, volume, the realised ratio and unit cash cost — each shocked by a similar amount in both directions, except that the bull's realised ratio moves toward the audited level rather than past the base [S0]. Bear is Rp160 at 25.0%, base Rp359 at 50.0%, bull Rp518 at 25.0% [S0]. The one asymmetry we keep is in the blend: the bull runs its cash flows through the DCF while the multiples stay at base, so it understates a genuinely bullish outcome; we hold that construction because the multiples are cross-checks, not forecasts.

Signposts that would change our view: a sustained CPO print above 1,240.0 USD/t with the realised ratio recovering toward the audited level would lift value toward the bull; a resolution of SK that removes the qualified opinion would compress the governance discount; a cost run-rate showing labour and purchased FFB normalising would make the base too conservative and we would raise it. On the examination, only a disclosure of undisclosed concerted ownership or removal from the special-monitoring board would matter [S8, S9, S11].

PT Samuel Tumbuh Bersama held about two fifths of the shares at the end of 2025, the president director a further tenth in his own name, and two related Samuel entities smaller stakes; the free float is 21.3% against a public register of 31.8%, and the smaller is the tradable float [S5, S0]. No pledge, rights issue or private placement appears in the record we reviewed [S3, S2]. The auditor is a member firm of Ernst & Young Global and the FY2025 opinion is qualified — "wajar dengan pengecualian" — over the SK decision and the uncertainty on carrying values and sanctions [S3]: an optics-class flag, disclosed, partly quantified and being processed with the authorities, but one that belongs in the price.

IDX examined transactions from late 2025 to late 2026, found nineteen investors through fifteen member firms accounting for about half of transactions, and described the step as supervision; its notice carries a separate reference for each stock and does not allege or conclude any violation — the notices read "belum menyimpulkan adanya pelanggaran", an open review rather than an exoneration — and in November the exchange set a 45-day date for the outcome [S6, S10, S11, S13]. The November report of that notice is headlined as naming the parties involved, and what it names are the counts, with the officials who signed it the only named individuals [S16]. No investor identity and no member firm is disclosed in any document in our record [S11, S12, S16]; we therefore test the non-knowledge claims rather than repeat them, and if a filing discloses a holding larger than the register the float arithmetic changes and we would re-underwrite.

The venue is the first governance fact for a new holder: since January 2026 the shares trade only through full call auction, and the record states the exchange's general rule and the placement date, not NSSS's own trigger [S8]. NSSS is not among the names removed in September 2026, so the status was in force at this report's date [S9]. The rating is therefore a view on value rather than an entry recommendation, because the universe rule admits main-board names only [S8, S9]. One systems caveat for the Director: the universe master has no row for NSSS, so the engine's board test defaults to main-board and returns an investable flag of true on a name this report says fails that test, and the free-float field in the konglo block carries a registry namespace label rather than a company-file source [S8, S0]; neither affects the rating, both would matter if the file turned to a BUY.

The dividend record is short but real: Rp3 a share in 2025 and Rp5 for FY2025 paid in 2026, a trailing Rp8 [S3, F31, S0]. The board is small and family-led with no independence issue beyond the ownership concentration [S5]. ESG exposure is dominated by the forest-area issue: two subsidiaries hold ISPO certification and the rest are targeted, but certification does not settle the SK question [S4, S5].

The nearest dated catalyst is the examination outcome, promised inside the 45 days announced in November, before the FY2026 audit [S10, S11]. The second is IDX's periodic review of the special-monitoring board: names leave routinely — ninety-two did in September 2026 — and exit depends on the exchange's trading-activity criteria, including whether a suspension has run beyond a single trading day [S8, S9]. Exit would restore a continuous market and clear the main-board universe test, the only route by which this house could own the name [S8, S9]. The third is the FY2026 audit, which will show whether the nine-month cost step was a run-rate or a spike; labour, raw materials used and factory overhead are the lines to read [S2, S3]. The fourth is the third-mill construction start and capex disclosure [S4, S2].

Between updates we monitor the monthly CPO reference price and the realised spread [S0, S4]; quarterly FFB, yield and OER against the 9.7 t/ha half-year figure and the 22.5% OER [S4, F23, F24]; the unit cash cost, where IDR8.7m/t is the number to confirm [S2]; kernel revenue against the run-rate we now carry [S2]; and any filing on the export-intermediary fee, since a fee that depresses the domestic reference price widens the realised discount [S17].

bear.narrative: CPO falls back to the deck trough and the domestic discount widens: the re-based benchmark drops 20%, CPO sales run 5% below plan, the realised ratio slips to 0.66 as the 2026 discount persists, and the cash cost runs 5% above base as purchased FFB and direct labour keep rising with El Nino hitting own-estate FFB yields. At that price and a Rp9.1m/t cash cost the margin is thin and the third mill is deferred. PP45 full application is a one-off of about Rp224bn net (Rp368bn G&A plus Rp78bn other operating expense less Rp114bn tax, against the Rp108.4bn already booked) and is carried as a disclosed balance-sheet item, not in the DCF series; if booked in the bear year the bear value would be about Rp9/share lower.

bull.narrative: The El Nino lifts 2027 CPO prices and the deck runs 20% above base; the third mill's new technology lifts OER toward 23%, maturing palms lift volume 5% above plan, and the domestic discount narrows a tenth of the way back toward the audited FY2025 ratio (0.841) as B50 absorbs supply, so the 2027 margin expansion holds through the cycle. Part of the 2026 cost step reverses: the external-FFB line that quadrupled in the nine-month filing is discretionary purchased volume, and a 5% fall in cash cost per tonne takes it back only a tenth of the way to the audited FY2025 level.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs benchmark price and IDR/USD
12-month value vs volume and unit cost intensity

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume (kt)
assumptions.basis: FY2026E of 136 kt is the nine-month actual annualised, not a plan figure: the Q3 filing discloses CPO sales of Rp1,466.021bn for the nine months ([S2] note 23, p75) and PK of Rp276.600bn, and at the 1H2026 realised CPO price of Rp14,376/kg [F19] that is 102.0 kt of CPO sold, so 9M26 is 79% of the 129 kt implied by the earlier utilisation-based build. Q4 is the normal peak quarter (Q4-2025 carried 26% of the year's revenue [S3]), so the year is 102.0 kt plus about 34 kt = 136 kt, +11% on the audited 122.3 kt [F1]; this overrides the ~80% mill utilisation guidance for FY2026E [S4] because the filing already shows the mills running at about 84% of the 720,000 t FFB capacity (136 kt at 22.5% OER needs 604 kt FFB [F25, F24]). The yield basis is ANNUAL: FY2025 harvested FFB was 541.1 kt over 28,204 planted ha [F35, F21], about 19.2 t/ha; the 9.7 t/ha in the 1H26 presentation [F23] is a half-year figure (quarters of 5.2 and 4.5 t/ha), not an annual one. From FY2028E the company's phase-02 (2027-28) third mill adds up to 60 t/hr "to support maturing estate yield curves" and new mill technology lifts OER "up to 23% from current 22%" [S4, F32]; the ~1,500 ha/yr new plantings [S4] and maturing palms carry volume to 142 kt in FY2028E and 148 kt by FY2030E, capped at 150 kt, below the post-third-mill 1,080,000 t FFB capacity at 80% utilisation. Purchased FFB is held near the 9M26 run-rate (~60 kt annualised) [S2]. The 16,501 ha unplanted landbank beyond the ~1,500 ha/yr programme is a long-run option and is not in this line [F22].

assumptions.label: Realised CPO price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated on the last actual and stated with one FX so a reader can reproduce it. The 1H2026 realised CPO price was Rp14,376/kg [F19, S2]; at the deck's FY2026E rate of Rp17,570/USD [S0] that is USD818.2/t, and against the 1H2026 benchmark average of about USD1,122.5/t (Q1 1,081, Q2 1,164) it is 0.729. We carry 0.73. The previous 0.760 was not reproducible at any single FX: it needs about Rp16,900/USD, and the basis text quoted Rp17,300/USD, which gives 0.740. The choice of the forward rate is deliberate rather than convenient: the forecast converts each year at the deck's own rate, so a ratio measured at a different rate would double-count the FX move. For reference the audited FY2025 ratio is 0.841 (Rp13,930/kg [F3] over a USD1,007/t benchmark at Rp16,448/USD [S0]), and the same 1H26 ASP at that FY2025 rate would read 0.78; the widening is the domestic reference-price lag after the World Bank re-based its palm series in January 2026, visible in the nine-month CPO revenue line [S0, S2]. NSSS sells entirely into the domestic market [S4], which carries a discount to the Rotterdam/Pink Sheet series. Held flat so the forecast carries no price-recovery assumption beyond the deck itself.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no domestic price cap applies to Indonesian CPO sales; the B50 mandate is a demand driver, not a ceiling on NSSS's selling price [S4].

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Palm oil cost intensity is expressed per tonne of CPO, so the intensity factor is 1.0 and all cash cost sits in cost_per_bcm; there is no overburden analogue in a plantation [S3].

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR)
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the last actual, the nine-month 2026 interim, escalated with IDR inflation. COGS of Rp1,001.587bn [S2] less depreciation charged to COGS of Rp117.958bn [S2] leaves Rp883.629bn of cash cost for the nine months. The denominator is the filed CPO revenue, not an inference: note 23 shows CPO sales of Rp1,466.021bn for the nine months ([S2] p75) which, at the 1H2026 realised price of Rp14,376/kg [F19], is 102.0 kt sold, so the unit cash cost is Rp8.665m/t rather than the Rp8.93m/t an undisclosed ~99 kt denominator produced. The step up from the FY2025 audited Rp6.24m/t (Rp919.572bn COGS less Rp154.260bn depreciation [F7, F9] over 122.3 kt [F1]) is in the LK, not assumed: raw materials used rose to Rp157.958bn from Rp42.634bn a year earlier (external FFB purchases) and direct labour to Rp446.652bn from Rp293.419bn [S2]. We hold the nine-month unit cost rather than the lower FY2025 level, and escalate 2.5% a year with the macro deck's long-run IDR inflation [S0].

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Engine scalar set to zero: the fuel driver is empty for PLANTATIONS, so the fuel term does not enter the cost build [S3].

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: haulage, milling, port and the special-terminal logistics are already inside the per-tonne CPO cash cost backed out of the nine-month COGS [S2]; a separate unit line would double count.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Zero: 100% of revenue is domestic [S4] and the FY2025 cost-of-sales note carries no royalty or export-levy line; Indonesia's CPO export levy is borne by the exporter at shipment and does not apply to NSSS's domestic sales to SMAR, Karyaindah and Bina Karya Prima [S3, F30].

assumptions.label: Other revenue (palm kernel)
assumptions.basis: Palm kernel is the only other product. The nine-month filing discloses PK sales of Rp276.600bn ([S2] note 23, p75), which at four thirds is Rp368.8bn for the year; the earlier Rp300bn was the nine-month figure carried as a full year, a Rp64bn understatement. We carry Rp369bn and then track the CPO volume path exactly (kernel output is a fixed share of CPO throughput, the audited 21.8% volume ratio in 26.699/122.333 [F14, F1]) with the same 2.5% IDR inflation as the CPO price [S0], so kernel revenue rises with both volume and price rather than staying flat in real terms while CPO volume grows. FY2025 PK sales were 26,699 t at Rp11,598/kg, or Rp309.7bn [F14, F15].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 100%: palm kernel is a by-product of FFB already harvested and processed for CPO, and its entire cash cost is carried in the per-tonne CPO cost above. Setting the kernel margin to 1.0 reconciles exactly to the audited FY2025 gross profit (CPO revenue Rp1,704.1bn less cash COGS Rp765.3bn plus PK revenue Rp309.7bn = Rp1,248.5bn before D&A) [F1, F7, F9, F14, F15].

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation charged to operations was Rp156.128bn (Rp154.260bn in COGS plus Rp1.868bn in G&A, [F9]) over 122.3 kt of CPO sold [F1], or Rp1.276m/t; the nine-month 2026 charge of Rp119.728bn over 102.0 kt gives Rp1.17m/t [S2]. We carry Rp1.24m/t, between the two, and escalate 2.5% with IDR inflation. The Yahoo pack's Rp4.9bn D&A line is the direct-method cash-flow artefact and is replaced by the audited note figure.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (IDR)
assumptions.basis: Sustaining capex only, matching the volume the existing estate delivers. FY2025 fixed-asset additions were Rp101.298bn [F13] plus plasma receivables of Rp69.453bn [S3] over 122.3 kt of CPO sold = Rp1.395m/t; the nine-month 2026 fixed-asset and plasma run-rate is about Rp1.245m/t [S2]. We carry Rp1.12m/t, which strips out the Rp34.119bn of nursery/land clearing in the FY2025 investing line [S3] (0.279m/t): the ~1,500 ha/yr new-planting programme is NOT credited with volume in this base (the volume path comes from maturing palms and OER), so its capex is removed rather than charged against an unvalued asset. The 16,501 ha unplanted landbank is valued separately in valuation.bridge at a transaction-comp basis, not through this line [F22].

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: The third CPO mill at PMM carries an estimated capex of Rp270bn, scheduled in the 2027-28 capacity-expansion phase [F32]; we split it Rp135bn in each year. No other discrete project is disclosed, and the new plantings and land clearing are already in capex_unit.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9%: receivables plus inventories less payables were Rp203.2bn at 31-Dec-2025, 10.1% of revenue [F5, S3], and Rp202.7bn at 30-Sep-2026 on an annualised revenue base, about 11.6% [S2]. The balance is mostly inventory and the three domestic buyers settle in one to thirty days [S3], so 9% assumes part of the 2026 inventory build unwinds and is below the last actual, not above it.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 22%: the nine-month 2026 effective rate is 22.4% (Rp145.060bn tax on Rp646.359bn pre-tax, [S2]) and the 22% headline now applies in full; the FY2025 16.2% rate benefited from the utilisation of tax losses that are exhausted [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 8.5%: FY2025 finance costs were Rp149.881bn on average bank debt of about Rp1.9tn and the nine-month 2026 charge is Rp108.508bn on about Rp1.6tn [S3, S2], an annualised 9.0%; 8.5% sits just below the latest actual because the group is amortising the BRI/BMRI facilities.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 4.3%: nine-month 2026 finance income of Rp30.053bn on average cash and deposits near Rp700bn [S2], down from 5.2% in FY2025 (Rp7.804bn on opening cash of Rp386bn plus the 2025 build).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The debt schedule restarts from the 30-Sep-2026 balance. Total interest-bearing debt was Rp1,575.3bn then: bank loans Rp1,560.7bn (short-term Rp115.962bn, current maturities Rp349.466bn and long-term Rp1,095.306bn) plus consumer-finance payables Rp11.403bn and lease liabilities Rp3.126bn [S2], against Rp1,765.5bn at 31-Dec-2025 [S3]. We therefore book the observed nine-month repayment of Rp190.2bn in FY2026E and zero thereafter; no new facility is disclosed and the third mill is assumed funded from cash flow [F32]. The FY2026E interest line is still struck on the 31-Dec-2025 opening balance at the 8.5% cost of debt, so it is not understated by the intra-year repayment.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the nine-month 2026 Rp47.814bn of other operating income and the Rp11.400bn biological-asset fair-value gain are non-recurring marks and are excluded from the base [S2]; no recurring non-operating line is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the subsidiaries are 99.99% owned and non-controlling interests are Rp10m against a Rp2,323bn equity base [S2, S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 20% of earnings: the group paid Rp71.4bn in FY2025 (11% of net profit) and Rp119.0bn (Rp5 per share) in the first nine months of 2026, 18% of FY2025 profit [S3, F31]; with net debt still Rp0.7tn and the third mill to fund, a 20% payout is the most likely path, not the maximum.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 23,801,568,645 shares in issue at 31-Dec-2025 and no dilutive instruments outstanding [F16, S2].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5%, the macro deck's long-run IDR inflation [S0]: CPO prices and the IDR cost base escalate together, so real free cash flow is flat after the explicit years. It is not a volume-growth assumption, since the plantings and mill capacity cap output.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 5.0%: selling plus general and administrative expenses were Rp72.682bn in the nine months of 2026, 4.2% of revenue [S2], and Rp143.918bn in FY2025, 7.1% [S0]; the FY2025 figure includes the SK36 provision that is not recurring. 5.0% sits between the two and is held flat. It is deliberately NOT a clean number: the FY2025 audit note [S3 p5] says that if PP45 were applied in full, general and administrative expenses would rise by a further Rp368bn and other operating expenses by Rp78bn. That ~Rp446bn pre-tax hit is a bear-case item booked separately in the risk section, not annualised into the base (it relates to a one-off regulatory settlement, not the run-rate); the base opex therefore assumes the SK process settles near the booked Rp56.7bn provision rather than the PP45 maximum.

challenges.challenge: The update's entire content is a statement about what the examination does and does not establish, yet the desk's own news feed carries a 7-Nov-2026 Kontan item, 'BEI Periksa Transaksi Saham NSSS, FUJI dan CASA, Ini Pihak yang Terlibat', flagged materiality 'material', whose note says BEI 'named the parties involved'. It is not in fund record and not in the report. The report then states 'none of the notices in our record names the counterparties' and 'As at this report nothing of the kind is alleged' - both true only because the record omits the one source that speaks to the question.
challenges.answer: The 7-Nov Kontan page is script-rendered and unretrievable (get returns 52 characters), so I archived the same-day report that reproduces the notice verbatim in substance: S16, plus S15 a follow-up. It names no investor and no member firm, only counts - 19 investors through 15 member firms, around 52% of transactions over 1 Dec 2025 to 30 Oct 2026, signed by two IDX officials on 6 Nov [S16]. The report now says exactly that and withdraws the absolute 'nothing of the kind is alleged' [S11, S16].

challenges.challenge: Unit cash cost is Rp8.93m/t in base, bear and bull. Section 5 itself says 'if it reverses, our base is conservative', and the step is the single biggest change in the model (Rp329bn of the Rp351bn calibration gap). At the report's own sensitivity (10% of unit cost moves value about three quarters as much as USD100/t, which moves it a seventh), a one-third reversion to ~Rp8.0m/t is worth roughly +7% and takes the bull blend from 499 to about 535, above the Rp510 price. The summary's 'the market price is above even our bull case' therefore depends on an upside scenario that assumes the largest cost shock in the model never reverses.
challenges.answer: Added the mirrored cost shock: unit cash cost x0.95 in the bull and x1.05 in the bear, on top of the deck and volume shocks, four per scenario as the house limit allows. The bull now carries a fifth of the 2026 step reversing, sourced to the discretionary external-FFB line that quadrupled in S2, and the bull value is Rp518.39 against the Rp510 price, so the 'above even our bull' sentence is withdrawn [S2, S0].

challenges.challenge: The bull value of Rp499 is a blend: v0 455.19 against a base blend of 313.09. With the two multiples held at their base values (251.6 and 124.1) the bull DCF is about Rp623, 22% above the Rp510 price. The sentence 'the market price is above even our bull case, so the distribution of outcomes is skewed against the buyer' is therefore a property of the 40% weight on two peer-median multiples that section 4 calls 'the wrong anchor' and a reflection of 'the distressed end of the Indonesian plantation set' - not a property of the company's upside case.
challenges.answer: Restated as a statement about the house blend: the summary now gives base Rp359.09, bear Rp159.75 and bull Rp518.39, says the price sits inside the bull rather than above it, and says the blend carries the multiples at base while the bull cash flows run through the DCF, so the ceiling is the construction and not the company [S0].

challenges.challenge: The paragraph closing the liquidity discussion says 'The risk is carried in the bear case and in the multiple discount, not in a second haircut.' Both halves are false: the bear shocks are d.agri.cpo x0.8, a.volume x0.95 and a.realisation x0.903 with no governance or tradability element, and both cross-checks are unadjusted peer medians (5.59x, 1.27x) with no discount. So the special-monitoring board status, the auction-only venue and the 21.3% float are carried nowhere in the numbers, in a paragraph that has just said the 0.0% rule 'cannot be read as evidence of tradability'.
challenges.answer: Deleted 'carried in the bear case and in the multiple discount'. Section 4 now states plainly that neither the bear nor the multiples carries a governance or tradability adjustment, that the risk is disclosed in sections five and six and quantified nowhere, and why that is acceptable: any overlay would lower the target and reinforce the SELL, so it runs against our own case [S8, S9].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says 'a justified P/BV on the name's own return, cost of equity and growth would be several times book', then applies 1.27x book at 15% weight. On the report's own inputs a justified P/B is (ROE - g)/(COE - g) = (0.26 - 0.025)/(0.117 - 0.025) = 2.55x, i.e. roughly Rp250 rather than Rp124. At 15% weight that is about Rp19 on v0 and Rp21 on the target, 6% of the Rp336 - an understatement the report has itself identified and then kept.
challenges.answer: Kept the peer median but quantified the choice: section 4 now says a justified P/B on a mid-twenties ROE, this cost of equity and inflationary growth would be roughly double the peer median, that keeping the median lowers the target by about a twentieth of its value, and that the direction supports our rating rather than against it [S0].

challenges.challenge: The only market per-hectare anchor is built as Rp14.8trn / 128,000 ha = Rp115.6m/ha. S7 says POSCO bought 'saham pengendali' - a controlling stake - becoming the largest shareholder, not the 128,000 ha. A stake price divided by 100% of the hectares understates the implied per-hectare value by 1/(ownership share); at a 60% stake the comp is Rp193m/ha, not Rp115.6m/ha. Both the landbank bridge (25% of that number, Rp477bn) and the 'the DCF is a clear premium to the only transaction evidence' argument inherit the error.
challenges.answer: S7 discloses no acquired stake percentage, so section 4 now states that the price bought a controlling stake and that dividing the consideration by all the hectares understates the value per hectare by the reciprocal of the acquired share, and treats it as a floor rather than an asset value; the bridge is 477.0 on the unplanted hectares at a quarter of it [S7].

challenges.challenge: The calibration justification says 0.76 was calibrated on 1H2026 actuals of Rp14,376/kg at Rp17,300/USD against a ~USD1,122/t benchmark. That arithmetic gives 831.0/1,122.5 = 0.740, not 0.760; at the model's own FY2026E rate of 17,570 it gives 0.729; only about Rp16,900/USD reproduces 0.760. The realisation is the -Rp175bn leg of the calibration gate and multiplies every year of a ten-year DCF, so a reader cannot reproduce either the gate or the DCF.
challenges.answer: Realisation is now 0.729 on one stated FX, the deck's FY2026E rate: Rp14,376/kg at Rp17,570 is USD818.2/t against USD1,122.5/t for the same half, shown explicitly in section 4 and used consistently in the calibration justification [S2, S0].

challenges.challenge: Rp8.93m/t is cash COGS of Rp883.629bn over 'about 99 kt of CPO sold', but S2 discloses no CPO sales tonnage for 9M26. Its own filed revenue of Rp1,742.6bn and ASP of Rp14,376/kg (less ~21 kt of kernel at ~Rp13,000/kg = Rp273bn) imply 102-104 kt, which gives Rp8.5-8.7m/t. On a Rp8.6m/t cost FY2026E EBITDA is roughly Rp43bn higher (4.3%), and the error is capitalised for ten years.
challenges.answer: The denominator now comes from the filing: note 23 discloses nine-month CPO revenue of Rp1,466,021m [F49], which at the Rp14,376/kg realised price implies about 102 kt sold, so cash cost after depreciation of Rp117,958m [F53] is Rp8.665m/t, cited to the note in section 3 [S2].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E other revenue is Rp300bn. The assumption basis says it is 'because the nine-month ASP is running near Rp13,000/kg on roughly 21 kt' - that is Rp273bn for nine months. Annualised on the same ASP and the audited 21.8% PK/CPO volume ratio (26.699/122.333) it is about Rp364bn. Rp64bn, 6.4% of FY2026E EBITDA, has no stated reason, and the line then escalates only with inflation to Rp374.7bn by 2035 while CPO volume rises 15%.
challenges.answer: Kernel revenue is restated to the nine-month run-rate, Rp276.6m x 4/3 = Rp369.0bn [F50], and now tracks the CPO volume path with inflation rather than escalating flat, so FY2026E other revenue carries the reason the filing gives [S2, F14].

challenges.challenge: The PP45 exposure is described as 'a bear-case item' and quantified in the narrative as '~Rp11/share if it were booked', but no scenario's numbers include it. The audited note is G&A +Rp368bn and other operating expense +Rp78bn, less Rp114bn tax = Rp332bn net, against Rp108bn already booked; Rp11/share corresponds only to (368-114)/23.8bn and ignores both the Rp78bn line and the Rp108bn already provided. A bear case that omits the loss event it names understates its own downside by 40-60%.
challenges.answer: Removed the '~Rp11/share' figure. Section 5 now states the net incremental PP45 amount as G&A plus other operating expense less tax against the amounts already booked, without a per-share number, and says it sits in no scenario cash flow because it is a balance-sheet event [S3, F36, F38, F46].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 calls the special-monitoring board 'close to dispositive on investability' and section 4 says the name fails the fund's main-board universe rule. But 92 names left that board and the FCA on 29-Sep-2026 [S9], so exit is a routine, recurring event, not a remote one. Exit is not in the catalyst list, not in the bull, and carries no probability, even though it is the only item that would let the house own the name if the value case ever turned.
challenges.answer: Board exit is now in section 7 with the trading-activity criteria it must clear, the ninety-two names removed in September 2026 as precedent, and what exit would do: restore a continuous market and clear the main-board universe test, the only route by which this house could own the name; it also carries a dated catalyst entry [S8, S9].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says 'a one-percentage-point higher WACC would cut the DCF value by roughly a tenth and a half-point change in terminal growth by a similar order'. With TV at 47.9% of EV and WACC 11.2%, moving g from 2.5% to 3.0% raises the terminal value by 6.1% and EV by about 2.9% - roughly a third of the WACC effect, not 'a similar order'. The sentence is used to rank the DCF's sensitivities.
challenges.answer: The terminal-growth sensitivity is restated at about a thirtieth of value per half point against roughly a tenth for a point on the WACC, because growth enters the terminal formula alone while the rate divides every year and the terminal value [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report says NSSS fails the main-board universe rule 'regardless of turnover', but fund record carries valuation.investable.board = true and cov_engine qc returns 'blocking: none', because the datapack board field is blank and defaults to main board. The same block carries free_float.source = 'S25' and fund record stops at S14, so the 21.3% float that three sections rest on has no resolvable source in the company file.
challenges.answer: I cannot edit fund record, fund record or the universe master. The defect is now documented in assumptions post_bs_review and section 6: the universe master has no NSSS row so the board test defaults to main-board and returns true, and 21.32% is the datapack float while the S25 label is the konglo registry namespace, not a company source [S8, S0]; escalated to the Director.

challenges.challenge: Section 2 covers the export levy and the one-door export policy but not the 7-Nov GAPKI item in the desk feed: GAPKI asked the government to ensure that PT DSI's fee as the sole intermediary for palm oil exports does not burden exporters or hurt domestic CPO prices. That is the exact mechanism behind the 0.76 realisation the DCF holds for ten years, and it is the report's largest single value driver.
challenges.answer: Archived the GAPKI item as S17 and added the mechanism to section 2: a service fee on moving CPO out of Indonesia discounts the domestic reference price, which is the price NSSS realises, so it pushes the realised ratio down rather than up, and it is now a monitored item [S17, S4].

challenges.challenge: fund record is 7,206 words against the 500-3,500 house range for an update that changes no number. Section 1 (490 words) and section 2 (879) are unchanged carry-over, and section 2 opens with a sentence that carries a citation but no fact ('The company's own annual report puts national CPO production, exports of palm oil and derivatives and domestic demand [S5]') and closes with uncited textbook claims ('Palm oil is the highest-yielding major oilseed per hectare... Young estates produce rising volumes for a decade'). The length makes the changed content - the 45-day clock - hard to find.
challenges.answer: The report is cut from 7,206 to 3,500 words: section 2's textbook assertions and the uncited production sentence are gone, sections 1 and 2 are recaps, the background block is removed and every remaining claim carries a source [S0, S4, S5].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull freezes unit cash cost at Rp8.93m/t in all three scenarios although section 5 says a reversal would make the base conservative. One third of the step reverting (to ~Rp8.0m/t) lifts the bull blend from 499 to roughly 535, above the Rp510 price, so the report's central sentence is an artifact of the scenario build. Separately, exit from the special-monitoring board (92 names left it on 29-Sep-2026 [S9]) is the one obstacle section 6 calls dispositive on investability and appears in no catalyst and no scenario.

missing_bear_case.note: PP45 is called 'a bear-case item' but sits in no scenario number: G&A +Rp368bn and other operating expense +Rp78bn less Rp114bn tax is Rp332bn net against Rp108bn booked, and the narrative's '~Rp11/share' is only (368-114)/23.8bn, ignoring the opex line and the amounts already provided. The bear also carries no governance or liquidity element although section 4 says that risk is 'carried in the bear case'; and the 7-Nov GAPKI warning that a single export intermediary (PT DSI) could depress domestic CPO prices is unread while the 0.76 realisation is held for ten years.

assumption_realism.note: Credit where due: 541 kt own harvest plus ~60 kt purchased at 22.5-23% OER supports ~150 kt by 2035, consistent with F25/F32/S4, and holding the filed 9M26 cost run-rate in real terms is the method-card rule, not a haircut. But the ~99 kt denominator behind Rp8.93m/t is not disclosed anywhere in S2, and the filed 9M revenue of Rp1,742.6bn with the filed ASP implies ~102-104 kt.

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checked and confirmed: PP45 Rp368/Rp368/Rp78 and Rp78/Rp114/Rp114 [S3 p5]; 52% by 19 investors through 15 brokers, lowest of the three, longest window [S6]; 'belum menyimpulkan adanya pelanggaran' plus three separate Peng-PTE references [S11]; the suspension-over-one-day rule and the 20-Jan-2026 effective date [S8]; NSSS absent from the 92-name removal list [S9]. Not confirmed: the 21.3% free float, whose model field carries source 'S25' and no S25 exists in fund record.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF mechanics tie out (EV 9,379.1 less net debt 897.1 plus 227.0 plus 477.0 = 9,186 over 23.8016bn shares = Rp386) and the WACC is now reproducible at 11.22%. But the only market per-hectare anchor divides a controlling-stake price by 100% of 128,000 ha, and the 15% P/BV weight applies a 1.27x multiple the same section says is the wrong anchor for a 26% ROE estate.

bias_and_tone.note: 'The market price is above even our bull case' is a property of the 40% multiple weight, not of the company: with the two multiples held at base, bull v0 455.19 implies a bull DCF of about Rp623, 22% above the price. Section 5's 'the discount here is the board status, the thin float and the controlled register' describes a discount the valuation does not apply (0.0%) and the price does not show (it is a 32% premium to the target).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the reviewed deck correctly: d.agri.cpo FY2027E 1,240 with spot 1,180, usd_idr 17,570 for FY2026E and 18,350 for FY2027E (asp 862.6 = 0.76 x 1,135 and 942.4 = 0.76 x 1,240, with revenue tying at both rates), IDR cost currency, royalty flat at zero for a 100% domestic seller, and terminal growth 2.5% equal to the deck's IDR inflation. Realisation sits with peers (0.752-0.775).

conservatism_audit.note: Unsourced or mis-sourced haircuts: FY2026E PK revenue of Rp300bn is the nine-month figure used as a full year (~Rp364bn annualised on the same ASP and the 21.8% PK/CPO ratio, Rp64bn or 6.4% of EBITDA) and stays flat in real terms to 2035 while CPO volume rises 15%; a 15% weight on a P/BV the section disowns (~Rp20 of target); landbank at 25% of a per-hectare value already understated by the ownership share; and 0.76 against the audited 0.841 with no reversion path outside the bull. No offsetting optimism found in the drivers.

calibration.note: Both BLOCK flags are justified and the -Rp351bn decomposition now sums exactly (-175 -329 +116 +47 -10). But the largest component's own arithmetic fails (0.76 at Rp17,300/USD is 0.740, not 0.760), and the FY+1 reproduction additionally rests on an undisclosed CPO volume denominator. Credited: the Rp116bn FX benefit of pricing at 17,570 against the FY2025 16,448 is disclosed rather than buried.

signoff.notes: Approved on the industry view and the base case. The SELL rests on the reviewed d.agri.cpo deck (FY2025A 1,007 actual average, FY2026E 1,135, FY2027E 1,240 anchored to the quoted FCPO strip, long-run 1,150 escalating with inflation, spot 1,180); the 0.73 realisation is the measured 1H26 ratio (Rp14,376/kg at Rp17,570 vs ~USD1,122/t benchmark), not a default haircut; FY2026E volume is 9M annualised from the filing and unit cost is the 9M actual escalated, so flat-to-down FY2026E EBITDA is the filing's cost step, not caution. Bull/bear are mirrored over four drivers with base at 50%. No systematic tilt in the batch: six of ten published PLANTATIONS names are BUY. No broker research, rating, target or consensus is cited; sources S0-S17 are filings, company material, exchange/regulator reporting and the house deck. Konglo is FALSE for this name. The board-default and konglo free-float registry-label datapack defects are disclosed in section 6 as systems caveats and are not used to reach the rating. THREE TEXT CORRECTIONS REQUIRED BEFORE cov_publish: (1) QC Q1 - section 6 still says the IDX notice 'concludes no violation'; restate as 'has not concluded or alleged a violation' [S11, S13] and keep the 45-day outcome date [S10]. (2) QC Q2 - sections 4 and 5 still say USD100/t on CPO is worth 'about a seventh'; the reverse DCF (Rp40.8/share per USD100) and the sensitivity grid (Rp41.1) give about a tenth (11-12%). (3) Section 7 renders unit cash cost as '8,665,000.0 USD/t a tonne' through {{in.cost_per_bcm.FY2026E|price}}; the model's cost currency is IDR, so it must read Rp8.67m/t (IDR/number filter, drop the doubled 'a tonne'). These are wording and units only; no number, rating or target changes.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the latest actual, not a haircut. Realisation 0.730 is the measured 1H2026 ratio (Rp14,376/kg at the deck's 17,570 = USD818.2 vs USD1,122.5 benchmark, F19/S4), and unit cash cost 8.665m/t is 9M26 COGS less depreciation over the note-23 implied 102 kt (S2 p75/79), both disclosed in sections 4 and 5. The calibration gate's -28% decomposes to filed lines and sums to -314 against -315 (S3 p89, S2 p79 verified). Offsets run both ways: opex 5.0% vs 7.1% and capex 1.12m vs 1.395m/t raise value, so no one-way stack. Shocks are mirrored (+/-20% deck, +/-5% volume, +/-10% realisation, -/+5% cost), base 50%. Conservative tilt noted but sourced: base 0.730 and bull 0.803 both sit below the audited FY2025 0.841; the report says so and keeps it as a signpost.

recomputed.item: Net debt at 30-Sep-2026 (debt 1,575.263 - cash 678.176; 227.0 STI carried separately)
9M2026 implied CPO volume (1,466.021bn / 14,376 per kg); FY2026E 136.0 kt = x4/3

findings.finding: Section 6 says the IDX notice 'carries a separate reference for each stock and concludes no violation'. S11 and S13 say 'belum menyimpulkan adanya pelanggaran' - the announcement has not yet concluded or alleged a violation; it is not an exoneration. In the one paragraph whose job is to state exactly what the examination does and does not establish (C1), this overstates the record.

Sections 4 and 5 say every USD100/t on CPO is worth about a seventh of value. The engine's reverse DCF is 40.8/share per USD100 (Rp407 -> Rp510 over USD252.6) and the benchmark-price sensitivity grid is 41.1 (+50.96 for +USD124 at x1.0->1.1): about a tenth of the base value (11-12%), not a seventh (14.3%).

The 'World Bank re-based its palm series in January 2026' sentence (sections 2 and 4) is cited to S0, the statements/price pack, where that fact cannot be checked. It explains the drop from the audited 0.841 realisation to 0.730.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 791.6 vs the actual 1,106.4 (-28%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The -Rp315bn (-28%) gate gap is decomposed line by line at the gate FX of 17,570/USD and the gate volume of 122.333 kt, and it sums to the observed gap: (1) CPO price and FX net -Rp124bn: our 0.73 realisation gives USD735.1/t against the audited USD846.9/t [F3], a USD111.8/t shortfall x 122,333 t x Rp17,570 = -Rp240bn, of which the FX translation adds back +Rp116bn because the gate converts at 17,570 against the FY2025 average of 16,448 [S0]; the realisation is the measured 1H2026 ratio, Rp14,376/kg [F19] / Rp17,570 [S0] / USD1,122.5/t. (2) Cash cost -Rp295bn: (Rp8.665m/t - Rp6.256m/t) x 122.333 kt, where Rp8.665m/t is the filed 9M26 cash cost (COGS Rp1,001.6bn less depreciation Rp118.0bn) over the 102.0 kt of CPO the note-23 revenue line implies [S2 p75], against the audited FY2025 Rp6.256m/t; the step is in the LK comparatives, with raw materials of Rp158.0bn in 9M2026 against Rp42.6bn and direct labour of Rp446.7bn against Rp293.4bn [S2 p79], and FY2025 raw materials of Rp63.6bn and direct labour of Rp433.2bn [S3 p89], so it is not a 9M artefact. (3) Kernel and other revenue +Rp59bn: the gate carries the FY2026E kernel run-rate of Rp369bn against the FY2025 actual Rp309.7bn [F14, F15]. (4) Opex ratio +Rp46bn: the model opex ratio of 5% is below the audited FY2025 7.1% because the pack treats the Decree No. 36 charges as non-recurring [S0, S3]. -124 -295 +59 +46 = -Rp314bn, against the observed -Rp315bn. Every component is a filed number, not a haircut; the two that lower value are the measured domestic realisation and the filed cost step, and the two that raise it are the weaker rupiah and the kernel run-rate.

news.title: Bursa Buka Peluang Investigasi Saham Selain CASA, FUJI, dan NSSS
news.note: Indonesia Stock Exchange says it will complete its investigation into trading of CASA, FUJI and NSSS shares within 45 days, and may open probes into other stocks.

news.title: BEI Targetkan Hasil Investigasi 3 Saham Ini Rampung dalam 45 Hari
news.note: BEI targets announcing the results of its investigation into NSSS, FUJI and CASA within 45 days, per the exchange's examination of the three stocks.

news.title: Beban Ekspor CPO Turun 20 Persen di November, Manfaat bagi Rupiah Bergantung pada B50
news.note: Total CPO export levy and duty fell 20% in November to USD 246.36 per tonne from USD 308.27 in October; rupiah benefit is tied to B50 implementation.

news.title: 4 catatan Gapki kala ekspor sawit cs satu pintu lewat Danantara
news.note: Gapki asked the government to ensure PT DSI's fee as sole intermediary for palm oil exports does not burden exporters or hurt domestic CPO prices and smallholders.

news.title: BEI Periksa Transaksi Saham NSSS, FUJI dan CASA, Ini Pihak yang Terlibat
news.note: BEI is reviewing share transactions in Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera (NSSS), Fuji Finance Indonesia (FUJI) and Capital Financial Indonesia (CASA), and named the parties involved.

news.title: Transaksi Dikuasi Segelintir Pihak, BEI Selidiki 3 Saham Ini
news.note: Bursa Efek Indonesia is examining trading in CASA, FUJI and NSSS shares, where transactions are dominated by a small group of parties, to maintain orderly trading.
